claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the current release can be certified now on the basis of aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance, despite the legal intake triage regression, because certification can be defended through documentation and disclosure rather than stale approval alone.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and the material segment weakness is already disclosed or covered by approved mitigation.
Use noncompliant if available evidence shows the required disclosure or approved mitigation is missing at the time of certification.
Do not treat aggregate readiness, lack of severity-one incidents, prior approval, or informal monitoring comments as substitutes for the explicit policy requirement.
evidence_requests: Current release documentation or model-card text showing the legal intake triage regression is explicitly disclosed as a material limitation for the named launch use case.
Approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance from the appropriate owner covering the subgroup weakness before launch.
Evidence that the current release documentation reflects the current evaluation batch and retrieval configuration, not just prior approval context.
specific_concerns: The policy requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses to be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation before certification.
Admissible evidence shows a material subgroup weakness in legal intake triage and shows no reviewed mitigation, owner-accepted risk treatment, or disclosure language attached in the release thread.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate policy condition for disclosure or approved mitigation of the subgroup weakness.
Prior approval is explicitly stale relative to the current retrieval configuration change and current evaluation batch, so it cannot supply the missing policy predicate.
unsupported_claims: That certification is currently supportable on a documentation-centered path; the evidence shows what would be required, not that the required disclosure or approved mitigation already exists.

That the release can be certified now rather than only after the model card or equivalent release documentation is updated to disclose the legal intake triage limitation or an approved risk acceptance is recorded.
